sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
"to declare the action of respondent No.6 in deleting the offences u/s. 409, 416, 421,
423, 464, 503 R/w 34 IPC without any basis, without assigning reasons and evidence on record from the charge sheet in pursuant to the C.C.No.1142 of 2023 on the file of the learned Addl. XI Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar,Ranga Reddy District though there is primafacie established by the petitioner as illegal,
arbitrary, unconstitutional, biased, cryptic, collusive, without following due procedure, contrary to the provisions of Cr.P.C. violative of Principles of natural justice besides violative of Article 14 and 21 of the constitution of India and consequently set-aside charge sheet filed in C.C.No.1142 of 2023 on the file of the learned Addl. XI Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar, Ranga Reddy District by directing the respondents to conduct a fresh investigation by not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Police and file fresh charge sheet duly following due procedure of law."

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 7.
3.

It is the case of the petitioner that he was running a small Firm under the name and style of "M/s MNR Chalasani Associates" which is engaged in construction of multi-storied buildings by taking the land on development basis from the respective land lords against the sharing of developed built up space therein.

4. It is the specific contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that on 24.06.2021, the petitioner along with his father met respondent No.7 who is Manager of L.I.C., H.F.L., F.S.L.,
Secunderabad Branch regarding loan, as he is in need of Rs.50,00,000/- towards completion of construction of apartment project.
Later respondent No.7 informed that petitioner's file is under process and the said loan amount will be disbursed in a week.
The petition further disclose about the Memorandum of Understanding(MOU) which was entered between respondent No.7 and the petitioner and delay of sanctioning of the loan by respondent No.7.

Further upon enquiry it came to light that no loan was initiated by the 2nd respondent for Flats bearing Nos.201, 202, 301 and 302 and the cheque which was issued to him was stopped for payment, for which, the petitioner was constrained to approach the Police to prefer a complaint against the 7th respondent.

5. It is the specific contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the Police have not registered any crime against respondent No.7, therefore, he was constrained to file private Ch. Naga Anirudh, vs The State Of Telangana, on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173395322/
1 complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. before the VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar, who in turn referred the matter under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. to the Police to register the case against the 7th respondent for the alleged offences under Sections 405, 409, 416,
418, 420, 421, 423, 464 and 503 r/w 34 of I.P.C.

entities.text: VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Rajendranagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The 6th respondent after investigating the entire case laid a charge sheet deleting the offences under Sections 406, 409, 416, 418, 421, 423, 464 and 506 r/w 34 of I.P.C. Therefore, the present writ petition has been filed seeking direction for fresh investigation in the case and to set aside the charge sheet which was already filed deleting the said sections.
6. On the other hand, the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home contended that alternative remedy is available and petition itself is not maintainable.
7. As contended by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home once there is an alternative remedy available to the petitioner, the writ petition is not maintainable.

When the Police delete the names of the accused or the offences the petitioner is at liberty to file protest petition before appropriate Court, upon which, it is for the Magistrate to consider for further investigation or for passing appropriate orders.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner shall approach the concerned Magistrate by making appropriate application/protest petition challenging the deletion of offences by the Police in this case.
8. However, the petitioner is at liberty to file appropriate application before the concerned Court.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

G.ANUPAMA CHAKRAVARTHY, J Date:
